daily_brief: A devastating magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, killing at least 132 people and collapsing dozens of buildings across cities including Pereira and Cali [BBC, Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail]. In the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, Ukrainian drones struck deep into Russia's Tatarstan region, killing at least 13 people including a child near the Tanevo oil refinery—one of the deadliest single attacks on Russian soil since 2022 [BBC, France 24]. Separately, Russian missiles struck Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia, killing at least five [France 24]. In a significant blow to Russian political pluralism, a Moscow court barred Yabloko, the country's only registered anti-war party, from participating in upcoming parliamentary elections [BBC]. The Trump administration issued an executive order calling for a reduced childhood vaccination schedule and the separation of the MMR vaccine into three shots, drawing sharp criticism from public health experts who called the move dangerous and scientifically unfounded [ABC Australia, Al Jazeera]. Meanwhile, Trump Media & Technology Group reported a $238 million quarterly loss, with unrealized losses on digital assets accounting for most of the shortfall [Al Jazeera].

top_stories.headline: Magnitude 7.4 Earthquake Kills Over 130 in Western Colombia
bullets: A 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck Colombia's Chocó province at 07:34 local time, with the epicenter near San José del Palmar at a depth of 103km
At least 132 people confirmed dead, with over 480 injured and many still feared trapped under collapsed buildings
The city of Pereira reported at least 40 deaths and 65 collapsed buildings; Cali and other western cities also suffered significant damage
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency to expedite recovery funding

top_stories.headline: Ukrainian Drone Strike Kills 13 Deep Inside Russia in Tatarstan
bullets: Ukrainian drones struck Nizhnekamsk in Russia's Tatarstan republic, over 1,100km from the Ukrainian border, hitting the Tanevo oil refinery
At least 13 people killed including one child, with 75 injured; seven victims were Uzbek citizens staying in a hostel
The attack is one of the deadliest single strikes on Russian territory since the full-scale invasion began in 2022
Moscow vowed 'inevitable and severe punishment' for those involved; Kyiv confirmed targeting infrastructure supporting Russia's war effort

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized distance from border and civilian casualties; noted BBC could not verify Russian claims

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Reported within broader context of ongoing tit-for-tat strikes including Russian attacks on Kyiv

top_stories.headline: Moscow Court Bars Russia's Only Anti-War Party from Parliamentary Elections
bullets: Yabloko, Russia's only registered party opposing the war in Ukraine, has been barred from September's parliamentary elections by a Moscow court
The lawsuit was brought by pro-Kremlin nationalist party Rodina, accusing Yabloko of supporting an 'extremist organization' (the LGBTQ movement) and copyright infringement
Hundreds of supporters, many young, gathered outside the courthouse; crowds chanted 'Shame!' when the verdict was announced
Several Yabloko members had already been individually barred from running before the party-wide ban

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Detailed the legal pretexts used and public reaction outside courthouse

top_stories.headline: Trump Orders Reduced Childhood Vaccination Schedule, MMR Split
bullets: Executive order calls for immunizing children against 11 diseases instead of the current CDC-recommended 17, dropping vaccines for RSV, Hepatitis A and B, rotavirus, influenza, and meningococcal ACWY
Order directs separation of the combined MMR vaccine into three individual shots despite scientific consensus that the combined vaccine is safe and effective
Public health experts condemned the order as based on pseudoscience and warned it will harm children
Order also directs the health department to improve vaccine research, though vaccines are already extensively studied

top_stories.headline: Trump Media Reports $238 Million Quarterly Loss Despite Revenue Growth
bullets: Trump Media & Technology Group reported a net loss of $238 million in Q2 2026 against revenue of just $1.7 million
Most of the loss ($190.4 million) attributed to unrealized losses on digital assets and equity securities
Revenue rose 89% year-over-year, with $1.43 million from advertising and $179,500 from subscriptions
Total losses for the first half of 2026 reached $644 million; TMTG shares fell 8% following the filing

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Straightforward financial reporting with detailed breakdown of loss categories
